easa.q: ____ is the upward force on the wing acting perpendicular to the relative wind.
easa.explain: Lift is perpendicular to the relative wind; drag is parallel to it.

easa.q: To overcome ____ and move the aircraft forward, thrust is needed.
easa.explain: Thrust balances drag in steady level flight.

easa.q: An object at rest or moving in a straight line remains at rest or continues to move in a straight line until:
opts: acted on by some other force

easa.q: The ratio of the maximum load an aircraft can sustain to the gross weight of the aircraft is called:
The ratio of true airspeed to the speed of sound is known as:
The effect of a sweptback wing is a delay in the onset of ____ effects.
easa.explain: Sweep reduces the velocity component normal to the quarter-chord line.

easa.q: The most common high-lift device fitted to the aft edge of the wing which increases lift and drag is known as a:
easa.explain: Flaps sit on the trailing edge; slats on the leading edge.

easa.q: A ____ is a small airfoil section attached to the upper surface of a wing that promotes positive laminar airflow over the wing and control surfaces.
easa.explain: Vortex generators make small vortices that energise the boundary layer (EASA p. 3.18).

anderson.q: Piper Cherokee: S = 170 ft², b = 32 ft, W = 2450 lb, airfoil a₀ = 0.1033/degree and α_L=0 = −3°, τ = 0.12. Cruising straight and level at 120 mi/h at sea level. The geometric angle of attack of the wing is:
anderson.explain: C_L = W/(qS), then α = C_L/a + α_L=0 with the finite-wing a.
anderson.detail: AR = b²/S = 6.024; V = 176 ft/s; q = 36.81 lb/ft²; C_L = 0.3915; a = a₀/[1 + 57.3a₀(1+τ)/(πAR)] = 0.0765/degree; α = 5.117 − 3 = 2.12°. Using a₀ instead of a gives the wrong 0.79°.

anderson.q: For the aircraft of Problem 5.4 with an airplane span-efficiency factor e = 0.64, the induced drag is about:
anderson.explain: C_Di = C_L²/(π e AR), D_i = C_Di q S.

anderson.q: The speed of sound in air at 230 K (γ = 1.4, R = 287 J/(kg·K)) is:
A flow at 1 atm and 288 K; a Pitot tube reads 1.555 atm. The flow velocity (using the compressible subsonic relation) is:
anderson.explain: p₀/p = (1 + 0.2M²)^3.5, solve M then V = M·a.
anderson.detail: Solving (1 + 0.2M²)^3.5 = 1.555 gives M = 0.8199; a = √(1.4×287×288) = 340.2 m/s; V = 278.9 m/s. Incompressible Bernoulli gives 303.0 m/s, a large error at M ≈ 0.8 (Anderson 8.13).

anderson.q: The flow just upstream of a normal shock has p₁ = 1 atm, T₁ = 288 K, M₁ = 2.6. Just downstream, M₂ and p₂ are:
In incompressible flow the peak pressure coefficient of an airfoil is −0.41. Estimate the critical Mach number with the Prandtl-Glauert rule:
anderson.detail: Cp,cr(M) = (2/γM²)[((1+0.2M²)/1.2)^3.5 − 1]; equating it with −0.41/√(1−M²) gives M_cr = 0.7436 (numerical root).
